newsitem.title: FRANCE: Philippe Levrier named head of France 3 television.
newsitem.headline: Philippe Levrier named head of France 3 television.

text.p: The chairman of state-owned France Television on Thursday named Philippe Levrier to replace Michel Blanc as head of France 3, one of the group's two channels.
"Michel Blanc has resigned today and has been replaced by Philippe Levrier," Herve Bourges, chairman of the audiorvisual regulator CSA, told a news conference.

France Television said in a statement the change followed "a difference of opinion" between Blanc and chairman Xavier Gouyou-Beauchamps which led to the two deciding that "they could no longer work together".

According to Le Monde newspaper, Gouyou-Beauchamps was exasperated by Blanc's thorough but slow decision-making process ahead of key restructurings involving closer cooperation between France 2 and France 3.
Levrier, 47, was the managing director of Telediffusion de France (TDF), the television transmission and uplink services company of France Telecom.
Gouyou-Beauchamps had been general manager of France 3 from 1994 until he was called to replace Jean-Pierre Elkabbach at the helm of the group on June 2 last year.
Elkabbach resigned after a scandal over generous exclusive contracts with popular television stars.
France 2 is the main state-owned national channel competing with commercial broadcasters TF1 and M6 as well as pay-television group Canal Plus.
France 3 has a series of regional services.
